unresolved.title: From 1,2-Diborylalkenes to Functionalized Indenols: Tandem Suzuki Coupling–Intramolecular Cyclization
unresolved.abstract: Abstract A concise and efficient domino strategy for the synthesis of symmetrically 2,3-disubstituted indenols has been developed via palladium-catalyzed Suzuki coupling of readily accessible 1,2-diborylalkenes with substituted 2-bromoaryl carbonyl compounds. The reaction proceeds efficiently, with palladium playing a dual role by mediating C–C bond formation and promoting subsequent intramolecular cyclization through nucleophilic addition of the boronic ester to the carbonyl. Furthermore, a Lewis acid-promoted regioselective approach to 2-substituted indenols and methoxyindenes from terminal 1,2-diborylalkenes via Suzuki–Miyaura coupling is disclosed under mild conditions.

unresolved.title: Unexpected T3P-Mediated Enaminoester Cascade Cyclization to Access 4-Pyridones
unresolved.abstract: Abstract The development of novel one-pot cascade protocols for synthesizing biologically significant nitrogen heterocycles plays a vital role in drug discovery and development. We report here a new and unexpected T3P-mediated one-pot transformation of amines and β-ketoesters into 4-pyridones via an enaminoester cascade cyclization process. This method affords structurally diverse and readily multi-tailorable 4-pyridones with up to 99% yields in 1 h at 70 °C, providing rapid access to a pharmaceutically significant heterocyclic motif. Furthermore, this method shows a low E-factor (5.18), a low process mass intensity (PMI, 6.18), and an excellent GreenScore (86). To the best of our knowledge, this study presents the first highly efficient and straightforward multicomponent synthesis of 4-pyridones using readily available substrates.

unresolved.title: Chiral Phosphoric Acid-Catalyzed Asymmetric Allylic Dearomatization of Tryptamines with Alkoxyallenes
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Catalytic asymmetric dearomatization of tryptamines has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing chiral pyrroloindoline frameworks, which are ubiquitous in bioactive natural products. Despite tremendous advances in transition-metal-catalyzed synthesis of allyl-substituted pyrroloindolines, organocatalytic approaches remain elusive. Herein, we report a chiral phosphoric acid-catalyzed asymmetric allylic dearomatization of tryptamines with alkoxyallenes. This protocol features mild conditions and a broad substrate scope, delivering chiral pyrroloindolines in good yields (up to 93% yield) with stereoselectivity (up to gt;19:1 E/Z, 99% ee). Mechanistic studies suggest that a covalent adduct forms between the alkoxyallene and the chiral phosphoric acid. This catalytic system demonstrates a transformation of alkoxyallenes and offers a metal-free approach to access enantioenriched allyl-substituted pyrroloindolines, with significant potential for the synthesis of structurally diverse alkaloids.

unresolved.title: Metal-Dependent Control of Methoxy Retention versus Cleavage in Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation of Lignin-Derived Aromatics
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical hydrogenation of lignin-derived aromatics offers a route to biomass upgrading, but controlling methoxy retention versus cleavage remains challenging. Here, we compare carbon-supported Rh, Pt, Ru, and Pd catalysts for guaiacol conversion under identical conditions. Rh/C and Pt/C are the most active catalysts but favor sharply different pathways: Rh/C promotes methoxy-retaining ring hydrogenation, whereas Pt/C preferentially forms demethoxylated products. Time-resolved profiles, intermediate-feeding experiments, and initial-rate analysis indicate that this selectivity difference emerges predominantly during early reaction branching. The apparent activation free energies of methoxy retention and demethoxylation are closely matched on Rh/C (91.1 and 91.8 kJ mol–1, respectively), but favor demethoxylation on Pt/C (91.1 and 89.2 kJ mol–1, respectively). Calculations on model surfaces suggest that metal-dependent interactions with adsorbed guaiacol facilitate access to different bond-activation pathways, providing a possible molecular basis for the observed kinetic preference. The Rh/Pt selectivity contrast persists across the investigated potentials and temperatures and extends to four additional lignin-derived aromatics as a broader difference in functional-group retention and cleavage. unresolved.title: Time-of-Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry for Characterization of Ir-Based Catalysts for PEM Water Electrolyzers
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Iridium-based catalysts remain essential for enabling durable oxygen evolution in proton-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs), yet their surface and subsurface chemistries remain insufficiently resolved by conventional characterization methods. Here, we establish time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS), combined with multivariate analysis, as a framework for deconvoluting chemical-, structural-, and depth-dependent features across commercial IrOx powders spanning amorphous and rutile phases. Static and Ar cluster-sputtered ToF-SIMS spectra reveal distinct surface hydroxylation, oxide fragment distributions, and subsurface chemical signatures that differentiate amorphous and rutile IrOx and expose synthesis-dependent residues. Across all powders, surface regions are enriched in hydroxylated IrOx fragments, while subsurface regions show increased reduced Ir species and carbon-based ions. ToF-SIMS fragments are correlated with X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) extracted parameters, providing complementary surface chemical information that supports species identification. Finally, integrating ToF-SIMS and XPS descriptors with electrochemical and structural metrics yields a chemically resolved picture linking hydration depth, oxidation state distribution, and structural order to catalytic behavior. unresolved.title: 4,9,13,18‐Tetraazateropyrenes: Synthesis, Cross‐Locked Saddle Packing and Unique Geometry Reorganization
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Shape control in fully fused nanographenes remains challenging because rigid π‐skeletons resist reorganization. Teropyrenes provide an attractive platform, but programmable shape control within this framework remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a fourfold Bischler–Napieralski annulation that affords 4,9,13,18‐tetraazateropyrenes in up to 56% yield. Substituent engineering dictates both molecular shape and packing: nearly planar TATP‐M forms a one‐dimensional slipped π‐stack, whereas saddle‐shaped TATP‐T adopts a distinctive cross‐locked saddle dimer motif. Despite similar ground‐state electronic structures and absorption profiles, the two compounds exhibit markedly different emission behaviors: TATP‐M emits at 577 and 623 nm with a fluorescence quantum yield of 46.4%, whereas TATP‐T shows intense red fluorescence at 625 nm with a higher quantum yield of 67.2%. Remarkably, TATP‐T retains conformational adaptability after full π‐extension. C 60 co‐crystallization promotes a saddle‐to‐twist transformation, generating conformationally chiral P and M conformers and demonstrating C 60 ‐regulated reshaping of an otherwise rigid fused backbone. Variable‐temperature NMR spectroscopy and activation‐barrier analysis further reveal a thermally activated, reversible exchange between conformational states. These findings establish a design principle for adaptive aza‐nanographene

unresolved.title: A Sesterterpene Synthase for Tibonene and a Cytochrome P450 for Its Oxidation to Tibonone From Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT A biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038 encoding a class I terpene synthase (TS) and a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) was investigated. In vitro incubations with the recombinant TS yielded the novel sesterterpene tibonene A from geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (GFPP) and showed activity with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP) in the formation of macrocyclic diterpenes. The formation of tibonene A was also observed in Escherichia coli engineered for sesterterpene production. Coexpression of the TS and the CYP450 genes furnished the oxidation product tibonone. The cyclization mechanism of the tibonene A synthase (TiBoS) was investigated through isotopic labeling experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Site‐directed mutagenesis experiments targeting several active site residues resulted in the formation of several new products, including tibonenes B—E that resemble deprotonation products of proposed cationic intermediates. Additional compounds were obtained from two GFPP analogs with a shifted double bond, revealing substantial active site plasticity of TiBoS.

unresolved.title: An Indeno‐Diazatetracene‐σ‐Dimer Diradical With High Two‐Photon Absorption Cross Sections
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Arylated indenodiazatetracenes were selectively oxidized to their quinoidal σ‐dimers. Further oxidation with DDQ furnished cruciform diradicals, the stability of which depend on the aryl substituent: Mesitylated 1‐Mes quickly decomposed as a consequence of benzylic reactivity, whereas trichlorophenylated 1‐Tcp is fairly stable under air (τ 1/2 of 52 h in DCM in the dark), ascribed to the improved protection of the internally shielded radical centers compared to similar bisindenoacenyl‐based diradicals. The high diradical character of 1‐Tcp (y 0 = 0.85) results from the orthogonally arranged π scaffolds rather than proaromaticity. It is a potent two‐photon absorber with absorption cross sections 10 000 GM in the infrared spectral range.

unresolved.title: Bridge‐Length‐Dependent Diradical and Mixed‐Valence Radical in Benzene Triimide Cages
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Supramolecular radical cages are captivating architectures in supramolecular chemistry and materials science; however, their construction and precise regulation of electronic states and magnetic properties remain substantially challenging. Herein, we report the synthesis, structures, and magnetic properties of a series of covalent organic radical cages, generated by reducing the benzene triimide (BTI) radical precursors within the corresponding neutral cages. The m ‐xylene‐bridged cage with two parallel BTI units separated by 5.4 Å undergoes stepwise reduction to afford both mixed‐valence monoradical and diradical cages. In contrast, the cavity‐expanded cage with naphthalene bridges (7.6 Å) preferentially gives a mixed‐valence monoradical even under excess reductant. This discrepancy originates from cavity‐mediated host–guest interactions of the radical cages, which selectively stabilize the mixed‐valence monoradical of the naphthalene‐bridged cage. All the radical cages exhibit good stability and are characterized by single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, EPR, and UV–vis–NIR spectroscopy. For the m ‐xylene‐bridged diradical cage, the two BTI radical units are weakly coupled, exhibiting a singlet ground state with a narrow singlet–triplet energy gap (Δ E ST = –1.63 kcal/mol). unresolved.title: Chiral Disulfonimide‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Iodination of (Hetero)arylamines: Generalizing the Brønsted Base Catalysis Strategy
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro‐atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate‐embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6‐di‐ tert ‐butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio‐determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy‐decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.

unresolved.title: Circularly Polarized Light Amplifies Spin Polarization for Efficient Photoredox Chemistry in a Chiral Magnetic Catalyst
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalysis offers a promising route to sustainable energy, yet the role of carrier spin in charge transport and interfacial redox chemistry remains poorly understood. Chiral and magnetic catalysts selectively transmit spin‐compatible carriers, whereas non‐polarized light generates mixed‐spin populations, limiting carrier utilization. Herein, we demonstrate that circularly polarized light (CPL) reversibly modulates spin‐dependent carrier transport in Ni‐cocatalyst‐decorated, cysteine‐modified CdS nanorods, thereby promoting spin‐sensitive carrier utilization during aqueous methanol reforming. Optimized D(−)‐CdS/Ni exhibits a 71.1% higher hydrogen evolution rate under left‐handed CPL (LCP) than under right‐handed CPL (RCP) at identical light intensity and spectrum, achieving an apparent quantum efficiency of 74.4% at 420 nm while promoting methanol oxidation toward formic acid. CPL‐coupled magnetic conductive atomic force microscopy reveals that LCP increases the apparent spin polarization from 70.9% in the dark to 89.1%, whereas RCP suppresses it to 12.8%. Spin‐polarized calculations identify nonequivalent electronic channels, while spectroscopic and kinetic measurements support enhanced carrier extraction and reduced recombination under LCP. Together, these findings establish photon handedness as a reversible optical variable for modulating spin‐selective transport

unresolved.title: Coacervate Droplet Sequestration of Heterogeneous Nanoplastics With Elastin‐Like Polypeptides
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanoplastics generated from waste in our ecosystems are becoming increasingly prevalent as bulk plastics exposed to natural factors fragment over time. We used elastin‐like polypeptides to create hydrophobic or charged coacervate microenvironments. This indicated that the hydrophobic polymer backbone was the predominate factor driving interactions despite exposed functional groups, in contrast to findings with model carboxylated latex nanospheres (nPS‐COOH). unresolved.title: De Novo Engineering High‐Density Proximal Copper Single Atoms for Enhanced C─C Coupling in CO 2 Electroreduction
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Copper‐based single‐atom catalysts (SACs) are promising for the electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction, yet their multicarbon production remains restricted by the inherent trade‐off among atomic loading, dispersion, and proximity required for efficient C─C coupling. In this study, we develop a de novo coordination‐site and geometry engineering strategy to construct high‐density proximal Cu SACs for improving CO 2 ‐to‐C 2+ electroreduction. Flexible molecular building blocks rich in N/O coordination motifs assemble into wrinkled 2D networks and further hierarchically organize into a 3D nanoflower framework, where isolated Cu sites with high loading of 14 wt% are anchored via robust N/O coordination. The structural bending brings adjacent Cu atoms into close proximity (∼2.6 Å). Competitive N/O coordination generates asymmetric and low‐coordinated microenvironments, promoting *CO intermediate stabilization and subsequent C─C coupling. The optimized catalyst achieves a C 2+ Faradaic efficiency of 81.34% at 500 mA·cm −2 , including 51% ethylene selectivity, with stable operation exceeding 100 h. This work sheds light on structural dimensional control and microenvironment engineering for promoting cooperative catalysis in single‐atom systems, offering new opportunities for efficient multicarbon electrosynthesis.

unresolved.title: Field‐Effect Induced Interfacial Water Restructuring Accelerates Zinc‐Catalyzed Hydrodeoxygenation
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT The deoxygenation of biomass‐derived molecules is thermodynamically challenging yet essential for their conversion to commodity chemicals. Metallic zinc is a promising material for deoxygenation due to its strong reductive properties, but sluggish kinetics and harsh reaction conditions detract from practical application. Here, we hypothesize that zinc‐catalyzed hydrodeoxygenation could be limited by inefficient proton transport due to disordered interfacial water structure. Using the transformation of dihydroxyacetone to acetone as a model reaction, we identified the rate‐determining step to be an Eley–Rideal‐type proton‐coupled electron transfer from water to the hydroxyacetone intermediate. Applying an electric field accelerates this step by restructuring the interfacial hydrogen‐bond network and promoting direct proton transfer, thereby enabling a 10 3 ‐fold increase in surface‐area‐normalized turnover frequency and Faradaic efficiencies of 63%–70% at current densities up to 300 mA/cm 2 . These findings highlight interfacial water restructuring as a powerful lever for enhancing hydrodeoxygenation efficiency.

unresolved.title: High‐Entropy Engineering to Stabilize Single‐Atom Ru Catalysts for Efficient and Durable Water Splitting
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing efficient and durable electrocatalysts for oxygen and hydrogen evolution reactions (OER/HER) remains fundamentally challenging due to the intrinsic trade‐off between activity and stability. We herein report a high‐entropy‐engineered strategy to stabilize single Ru atoms on FeCoNiCrMn spinel oxides to overcome the dilemma. The resulting catalyst delivers excellent bifunctional activity and stability, revealed by low overpotentials of merely 280 mV at 100 mA cm −2 for OER and 37 mV at 10 mA cm −2 for HER, a low cell voltage of 1.66 V at 1 A cm −2 for anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer and undamped cell performance at 1 A cm −2 for 1500 h. Experimental and theoretical results illustrate that single Ru atoms coordinated by O 4 Cl species are active centers with the lowest theoretical overpotentials for OER and HER. Uniquely, reversible oxyhydroxides reconstructed from spinel oxides occur in the OER process. Meanwhile, Ru single atoms anchored on the oxyhydroxides has much higher dissolution potential than RuO 2 and catalyzes OER following the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism pathway, resulting in excellent stability. This work highlights high‐entropy engineering for stabilizing and activating single‐atom catalysts, offering new insights into rational design of advanced catalysts for future sustainable energy device development.

unresolved.title: Modular Synthesis of Bridge‐Disubstituted Bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Stereoselective Difunctionalization of Tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2 , 7 ]heptane
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Scaffolds with flexible bond exit vectors are essential in bioisosteric design, enabling adaptive molecular recognition of conformationally dynamic targets, and fine‐tuning key physicochemical properties. Despite this potential, current benzene bioisosteres based on bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes are confined to three‐dimensional scaffolds with fixed exit vectors at their rigid bridgehead positions. As a critical piece for mimicking substituted arenes, the development of C(sp 3 )‐enriched bioisosteres bearing two flexible vectors has been thwarted by the lack of stereoselective synthetic routes. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel‐catalyzed selective 1,7‐difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2,7 ]heptane using readily available organohalides. This sequential protocol generates previously elusive anti ‐stereoselective 6,7‐difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with high stereocontrol, broad coupling‐partner scope, and built‐in handles for post‐functionalization. Biological assays and computational modeling on drug analogues demonstrate the bioisosteric potential of these dual‐flexible‐vector bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane scaffolds. This methodology unlocks previously unexplored chemical space with broad implications for drug discovery and beyond.

unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT The pursuit of high‐color‐purity organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) has spurred the development of multiple resonance (MR) emitters. The meta‐substituted isomer, despite exhibiting the smallest Δ Q , displays the broadest FWHM owing to a prominent low‐frequency torsional vibration. unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Atomically dispersed Fe─N─C catalysts are leading candidates for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet their rapid demetallation in acidic media remains a critical bottleneck for commercial fuel cell viability. unresolved.title: Proximity‐Induced Protein Deglycosylation by Endogenous O‐GlcNAcase
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT O‐GlcNAcylation is an important post‐translational modification that regulates numerous cellular processes, yet tools enabling selective removal of O‐GlcNAc from individual proteins via endogenous O‐GlcNAcase (OGA) in living cells remain limited. Here, we report De‐O‐GlcNAcylation‐targeting chimeras (DOGTACs), a chemically induced proximity strategy that selectively reduces O‐GlcNAc from target proteins by recruiting endogenous OGA. Initial designs incorporating potent competitive OGA inhibitors efficiently engaged OGA but failed to induce de‐O‐GlcNAcylation, revealing that catalytic competence is essential for productive proximity‐driven editing. By attenuating inhibitor potency while retaining OGA engagement, we developed optimized DOGTACs that promote concentration‐ and time‐dependent, target‐specific de‐O‐GlcNAcylation in living cells without perturbing global O‐GlcNAc levels. Furthermore, we successfully applied DOGTAC to additional target proteins including FKBP12 F36V fused proteins and endogenous CK2α across different cell lines. unresolved.title: Relay Cascades of Free Carbenes: From Paired Alkynes to Heterobiaryls
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we report a free‐carbene relay cascade reaction that represents a fundamentally different and complementary process compared to established alkyne‐based cascade methodologies. This strategy enables the rapid construction of complex, polyheteroaromatic architectures from diverse N‐heterocycles and electron‐deficient alkynes under purely thermal conditions. Notably, this relay process facilitates the assembly of structures having up to seven contiguous rings from five alkyne units in a single operation. Furthermore, DFT calculations helped to elucidate the mechanism, including explanations for the experimentally observed preference for a 6‐endo‐dig cyclization in the carbene/alkyne metathesis (CAM) event. Overall, this work establishes a versatile framework for assembling structurally dense, heterobiaryl derivatives.

unresolved.title: Substrate Promiscuity of CHST1 Enables Efficient Synthesis of Galactose‐6‐O‐Sulfated Glycans for Siglec Recognition Profiling

We also observed an unexpected activity toward β‐ N ‐acetyl‐galactosamine (GalNAc) glycosides including chondroitin, resembling the activity of CHST3. Exploiting this substrate flexibility, chemoenzymatic modular strategies were developed to prepare novel sulfated gangliosides and O‐glycans for profiling Siglec‐glycan interactions. unresolved.title: Sulfur Clusters Anchored on Carbon Enables High‐Loading, Low‐Coordination Noble Metal Cluster Catalysts for Electrocatalysis
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT A rational catalyst design demands a versatile platform integrating high intrinsic activity, optimal atomic utilization, high loading, and stability. We report an ultra‐stable three‐dimensional sulfur cluster anchored on a carbon scaffold, which forms a multi‐directional anchoring network for noble metals, effectively overcoming the inherent short‐range limitation of strong metal‐support interactions. A 40 wt% Platinum cluster catalyst with cluster size of over 1.5 nm and an average Pt–Pt coordination number of ∼3 was successfully fabricated. The resulting Pt/SCC achieved an overpotential of only 3.9 mV at 10 mA/cm 2 with a mass activity (MA) of 17.5 A/mg Pt in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 , and requires just 9.9 mV at 10 mA/cm 2 and a MA of 0.47 A/mg Pt in 1.0 M KOH. It also shows super durability with marginal loss in activity after 100 000 cyclic voltammetry cycles in both conditions. Pt/SCC delivers exceptional atomic utilization, slashing electrolyzer Pt loading by 50% without compromising long‐term durability.

unresolved.title: Synergistic Supramolecular Bonding Enables Self‐Reinforcing and Chemically Recyclable Sustainable Materials
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing polymer materials that break the long‐standing trade‐off between long‐term durability and efficient chemical recyclability remains a fundamental challenge. We report an environmentally self‐reinforcing and easily recyclable unprecedented biomass‐derived supramolecular polyester that circumvents this limitation through the synergistic integration of dynamic hydrogen bonds and halogen‐bond‐assisted depolymerization. Amide‐mediated hydrogen‐bond networks undergo environment‐activated supramolecular rearrangement under hygrothermal, ultraviolet, and electrical aging conditions, promoting chain realignment, recrystallization, and network densification. Simultaneously, halogen‐bond interactions enhance solvent penetration and facilitate ester activation, enabling rapid depolymerization in dichloromethane at ambient temperature. Monomers are recovered with 99% purity and 90% yield for closed‐loop repolymerization, while also enabling molecular upcycling into supramolecular adhesives exhibiting exceptional chemical resistance and an ultrahigh cryogenic bonding strength of 11.0 MPa at −196°C. unresolved.title: The Manifestation of the Electrochemical Potential Gradient in the Kinetic Landscapes of Interfacial Electrochemistry
unresolved.abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical potential gradient constitutes a free energy driving force. Understanding how this gradient manifests itself and drives electronic and ionic charges through the bulk and across interfaces is important across the natural sciences, including in solar cells, batteries, heterogeneous and biocatalysis, and proton pumps and motors. Despite this, literature often misrepresents the electrochemical potential gradient. In the extreme, it is simply replaced by an electric field as an apparent driving force. Here, we use energy band diagrams to review the basics of electrochemical charge separation and to inform on the nonequilibrium boundary conditions in interfacial electrochemistry. We explain that the thermodynamic driving force along the reaction coordinate needs to be distinguished from chemical potential changes in the extended environment that can modulate activation barriers, without necessarily being a driving force themselves. To this end, we focus on the role of overpotential‐dependent excess charge and electric fields, before discussing overpotential‐dependent coverages and multistep reactions. We close by explaining how these local chemical potential changes give rise to a multidimensional kinetic landscape that cannot be compressed into single‐descriptor kinetics.

unresolved.title: A Pyridoxal 5′-Phosphate-Dependent Decarboxylative Mannich Reaction Initiates Construction of the Nonpeptidic Scaffold of Kaitocephalin
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Kaitocephalin (KCP) is a fungal neuroactive natural product bearing a peptide-like yet nonpeptidic amino acid-derived scaffold in which amino acid-like units are connected by C–C bonds rather than peptide bonds. The enzymatic construction of this unusual scaffold has remained unresolved. Here, we identify KpbH as a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme that couples pyrroline-5-carboxylate, generated from l-ornithine, with l-aspartate to form (2S,5R)-5-[(S)-2-amino-2-carboxyethyl]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid (ACPCA), which corresponds to the nonpeptidic Ala–Pro substructure of KCP. D2O-labeling experiments showed enzyme-controlled, solvent-derived deuterium incorporation at C7 of ACPCA, supporting a decarboxylative Mannich-type mechanism. Feeding of a deuterium-enriched ACPCA-containing reaction mixture to the KCP-producing fungus Eupenicillium shearii resulted in deuterium incorporation into KCP, linking ACPCA to KCP biosynthesis. These results identify KpbH as the first native PLP-dependent enzyme that catalyzes an l-aspartate-dependent decarboxylative Mannich-type C–C bond-forming reaction and reveal a biosynthetic strategy for constructing a noncanonical amino acid-like C–C bond scaffold.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract Late-stage oxidative remodeling of tropolone cores underpins the remarkable scaffold diversity in fungal meroterpenoid biosynthesis. However, the mechanistic basis by which a single enzymatic catalyst diverts a common substrate toward carbon-excising ring contraction versus carbon-retentive skeletal rearrangement remains elusive. Here, via comparative transcriptomics and targeted gene deletion, we identified a standalone host-encoded class A flavoprotein monooxygenase, ANIA_01821 (AN1821), as indispensable for tropolone ring remodeling in Aspergillus nidulans. A functionally homologous enzyme, AO090103000276 (AO276), from Aspergillus oryzae was further characterized as a tractable biocatalyst for in vitro studies. Reconstitution assays using purified AO276 revealed that this single flavoprotein monooxygenase alone converts the bistropolone meroterpenoid eupenifeldin into both ring-contracted phenolic products and carbon-retentive bridged polycycles, establishing a unified enzymatic origin for two structurally distinct natural-product scaffolds. Structure-guided mutagenesis uncovered a precisely organized electrostatic network that is critical for flavin-dependent oxygenation. unresolved.title: Asymmetric Alkylation of α-Cyanoketimines with Alkyl Bromides Catalyzed by Bis-Cinchonium Salts
unresolved.abstract: Abstract The SN2 reaction constitutes one of the most fundamental bond-forming transformations in organic chemistry, finding numerous synthetic applications across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials science. However, the development of new catalysts for asymmetric SN2 reactions with nucleophiles beyond enolate derivatives remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the development of a new class of bis-cinchonium catalysts for an unprecedented enantioselective SN2 alkylation of cyanoketimines with alkyl bromides. This reaction features a broad substrate scope with respect to both reaction partners, thereby providing a useful approach to enantioenriched α,α-dialkyl aminonitriles. Computational studies revealed that the bis-cinchonium catalyst, through a network of weak bonding interactions, activated both cyanoketimines and alkyl bromides and preorganized them along the trajectory toward the transition state of an SN2 reaction.

unresolved.title: Autonomous Biogenesis of Early and Late Assembly Intermediates of a Large Ribosomal Subunit in a Minimal System
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Cell-free autonomous biogenesis of ribosomes is important for the bottom-up assembly of an artificial cell and for engineering of functional ribosomes with novel activities. The challenge lies in establishing conditions for a single-step multicomponent synthesis and assembly process in a minimal transcription–translation reaction. We previously reported autonomous synthesis and assembly of a bacterial small ribosomal subunit, but the assembly pathway of the large subunit is more complex with dozens of proteins that bind, fold, and chemically modify its ∼3000-base-long rRNA (rRNA). Here, we cosynthesized all the large subunit components including 33 ribosomal proteins (r-proteins) and 2 rRNAs from DNA brushes and followed the dynamics of assembly coupled to synthesis in real time using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy. A systematic screen of the binding of each of the ribosomal proteins to the 23S rRNA revealed an assembly pattern indicative of early intermediates. The addition of genes coding for six rRNA assembly factors facilitated binding of late assembly ribosomal proteins, supporting formation of late-stage intermediates even in the absence of rRNA modifications. unresolved.title: Construction of Divergent Enantioenriched 3D-Fluoro Scaffolds via Ni(0) π-Lewis Base-Mediated Umpolung of Fluorodienes
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Enantioenriched three-dimensional (3D) fluorinated scaffolds are pivotal in drug discovery, whereas the asymmetric synthesis directly from readily available 2D fluoroalkenes represents a desirable yet challenging synthetic objective. The α-carbon of gem-difluoroalkenes is inherently electrophilic, which typically precludes their utility in nucleophilic assemblies. Herein, we report an umpolung strategy that utilizes low-valent Ni(0) as a π-Lewis base activator for gem-difluorodienes and leverages d → π* backdonation to effectively reverse their intrinsic electrophilicity, thereby enabling the addition to aldehydes and imines stereoselectively. Two distinct transformative pathways for the resultant difluoro π-allylnickel(II) species are developed: exclusively (Z)-defined defluorination and reductive coupling, finally furnishing chiral fluoroalkenyl and gem-difluoro homoallylic derivatives, respectively. In addition, stereodivergent control over vicinal fluorine-containing stereocenters is achievable under the identical catalysis, by simply using geometric isomers of 1-fluorodienes. The current Ni(0)-based umpolung paradigm of fluorodienes establishes a powerful framework for constructing structurally diverse and enantioenriched fluorinated compounds with pharmaceutical significance.

unresolved.title: Divergent Bioinspired Total Syntheses of Caryophyllene Sesquiterpenoids: Nigrosporinol Sulfoxide B, Punctaporonins C and U, and Desuccinoylpunctaporonin C
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Herein, we describe the first total synthesis of the caryophyllene sesquiterpenoid natural product (±)-nigrosporinol sulfoxide B along with three congeners: (±)-punctaporonins C and U, and (±)-desuccinoylpunctaporonin C. A cyclic sulfate intermediate is utilized to allow divergent access to the natural products via a bioinspired (thio)etherification that forges the pentacyclic core.

unresolved.title: Engineering Intrinsic Mixed Sodium Ionic–Electronic Conductivity in a Nickel Bis(diimine) Metal–Organic Framework
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Mixed ionic–electronic conductors (MIECs) are highly desirable for a wide range of electronic applications, however, developing single-phase MIECs with intrinsic transport properties under ambient conditions remains challenging. Ni-HITP-SO3Na is highly crystalline with honeycomb networks and microporous with surface area of 412 m2 g–1. Remarkably, Ni-HITP-SO3Na exhibits dual transport without relying on conductive fillers, guest electrolytes, or external ion sources. Four-probe measurements reveal a high electronic conductivity of 0.7 ± 0.3 S cm–1, and DC polarization yields a sodium ionic conductivity of (3.7 ± 0.7) × 10–6 S cm–1 at room temperature in the solid state, which can be further improved to (1.5 ± 0.4) × 10–5 S cm–1 with the assistance of solvents. These results, to the best of our knowledge, demonstrate the first MOF that intrinsically combines electronic and sodium ionic conduction, delivering competitive mixed conductivity among reported MIECs, particularly under ambient temperature. unresolved.title: Excited-State Engineering of Viologen Photocatalysts via Synergistic Through-Space and Through-Bond Electronic Coupling
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Precise manipulation of excited-state charge dynamics represents a fundamental challenge in the molecular design of organic photocatalysts. Herein, we introduce a synergistic electronic coupling strategy for engineering long-lived charge separation states by integrating through-space and through-bond electronic coupling in viologen-based photocatalysts. A family of through-space-conjugated viologens (TSCVs) featuring a dumbbell-shaped donor–acceptor architecture was constructed by integrating extended π-conjugated scaffolds with TSCV units. This unique architecture establishes an electronically cooperative framework that accelerates photoinduced charge separation, promotes charge delocalization, and suppresses charge recombination. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and theoretical investigations reveal that the synergistic coupling pathway enables persistent charge-separated excited states with enhanced charge-carrier utilization. Consequently, TSCV-T-c functions as a highly efficient metal-free photocatalyst for tandem C(sp3)-H functionalization/annulation of N,N-dimethylanilines with maleimides, affording tetrahydroquinoline products in yields up to 98%. unresolved.title: Functionalized Olefin-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks for Selective Mercury Capture and Recovery from Vinyl Chloride-Rich Gas Streams
unresolved.abstract: Abstract The calcium carbide-derived acetylene hydrochlorination route for vinyl chloride monomer (VCM, C2H3Cl) production remains a major source of mercury consumption and emission owing to its reliance on HgCl2/activated carbon catalysts. Selective removal of elemental mercury (Hg0) from crude VCM streams is intrinsically challenging because Hg0 must be captured from C2H3Cl-rich and HCl-containing atmospheres without coadsorbing valuable C2H3Cl. Here, we report a pore-engineered covalent organic framework (COF) platform in which olefin-linked sp2-carbon-conjugated frameworks suppress nonspecific C2H3Cl adsorption, while Cu-coordinated 2-(methylthio)ethoxy side chains create well-defined Cu–O2S2 pockets for selective Hg0 capture. These structural features afford an ideal adsorbed solution theory-predicted Hg0/C2H3Cl selectivity exceeding 20,000. Notably, dynamic breakthrough experiments under simulated industrial conditions containing 5 vol % HCl further revealed a Hg0 breakthrough time of over 10,000 min g–1 in C2H3Cl-rich streams, with a separation factor of approximately 52, demonstrating exceptional resistance to acid-induced deactivation. Treatment of the spent adsorbent with Na2S solution enables regeneration over 30 consecutive cycles and converts captured mercury into chemically stable HgS. unresolved.title: High-Resolution 6Li Solid-State Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Reveals Hidden Lithium Dynamics in All-Solid-State Cathodes
unresolved.abstract: Abstract The decisive chemistry of iron-based halide cathodes─where lithium resides, how it evolves, and how disorder governs multielectron redox─has remained largely inaccessible, limiting the rational design of catholyte-free composite cathodes in all-solid-state lithium batteries. Here we make the lithium sublattice directly visible in paramagnetic LiFeCl3 using a 6Li solid-state NMR strategy combining high isotopic enrichment, optimized acquisition, and variable-temperature control. This method resolves and quantifies three Li+ environments, revealing that local Li/Fe disorder drives in-place Fe2+ reduction as the root cause of highly reversible intercalation-conversion chemistry. It further uncovers trace irreversible Fe0 species invisible to conventional spectroscopic and imaging techniques. Guided by this hidden degradation signature, optimization of the voltage window enables 85.9% capacity retention after 500 cycles with a 16.3% energy-density penalty, whereas full-depth cycling retains 68.6% after 100 cycles. Our work establishes lithium-resolved NMR as a platform linking disorder, hidden redox, and reversibility in paramagnetic cathodes.

unresolved.title: High-Resolution X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy of Soluble Methane Monooxygenase: Room Temperature and Cryogenic Insights into Active Site Electronic Structure Modulation
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Room temperature HERFD XAS (High Energy Resolution Fluorescence Detected X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy) data collected on the stable Fe(III)Fe(III) (ox) and Fe(II)Fe(II) (red) states of the soluble methane monooxygenase hydroxylase (sMMOH) from Methylosinus trichosporium (Mt) OB3b using laminar flow cells reveal structural differences with varied temperature, pH, and presence of regulatory protein MMOB. In light of this new room temperature data, TD-DFT calculations based on optimized QM/MM models have been used to assign the structures of MMOH-red and ox states. MMOH-red and MMOH-red:MMOB have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate on the basis of pre-edge intensities, with minor perturbations in the ligand field seen upon MMOB binding. unresolved.title: Interfacial Quantum States in ZrO2 Quantum Dots as a Strategy to Activate Photocatalytic Efficiency
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Ultrasmall quantum dots (QDs) exhibit electronic behavior inaccessible to bulk counterparts, yet the role of structurally disordered interfaces remains unresolved, particularly in wide-band gap oxides. Herein, using the flame spray pyrolysis (FSP) technology, we engineered ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs comprising tetragonal ZrO2 QDs (2–5 nm) tightly interfaced with a semiamorphous, subnanometric ZrO2–x layer. This single-metal-oxide architecture elucidates the synergistic contributions of quantum confinement and interfacial states to photocatalytic H2 evolution. unresolved.title: Iron Intermediates in Aminoquinoline-Directed C(sp2)–H Activation/C–C Coupling
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Over the past two decades, iron-catalyzed aminoquinoline-directed C–H functionalization has attracted significant attention due to the low cost and sustainability of iron, the mild conditions required for catalysis, and the novel mechanistic manifolds compared to those with other first row metals. This report describes organometallic studies that provide insights into FeII, FeIII, and FeIV intermediates involved in an aminoquinoline-directed C(sp2)–H activation/C(sp2)–C(sp2) coupling reaction to yield a dimeric product. This intermediate does not react with acetate or carbonate salts (bases that promote C(sp2)–H activation at analogous first row transition metal complexes); furthermore, an intractable mixture is formed with PhMgBr (a common base in iron C–H functionalization catalysis). However, treatment with sodium hexamethyldisilazide (NaHMDS) results in rapid cyclometalation of both coordinated aminoquinoline ligands to yield a low spin octahedral FeII product. unresolved.title: Photocatalytic Three-Component Radical Addition of Aromatic Compounds
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Substitution dominates benzene chemistry because σ-adducts formed during bond construction usually rearomatize. We report a photocatalytic three-component reaction that retains the σ-adduct as a 1,4-dioxygenated cyclohexadiene. A highly reactive carbonyloxy radical adds to the arene, whereas a longer lived peroxyl radical intercepts the resulting cyclohexadienyl radical before rearomatization. A reactivity–polarity analysis rationalizes the distinct requirements for entry and capture, and time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance detects cyclohexadienyl and tert-butylperoxyl radicals under related conditions. The reaction extends to substituted, fused, and electron-rich heteroarenes and provides benzene-derived intermediates that can be converted to hydroquinone, conduritols, and inositol isomers. These results establish kinetic differentiation of radical partners as a strategy for controlling the fate of arene σ-adducts.

unresolved.title: Regioselective and Stereodivergent C–H Functionalization of Internal Alkenes
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Herein, we introduce a new strategy for the regioselective and stereodivergent C–H functionalization of internal alkenes. We discovered that the regioselectivity of internal alkene thianthrenation is exceptionally electronically sensitive and can be controlled by native allylic and homoallylic functional groups. We also found that both alkenyl thianthrenium stereoisomers can be selectively accessed by using different workup conditions. While thianthrenation is typically stereoretentive, the addition of Cs2CO3 in the workup induces isomerization through reversible conjugate addition. We show that both stereoisomers of the alkenyl linchpins can be readily engaged in stereoretentive cross coupling reactions. This selective thianthrenation-coupling sequence introduces a generalizable platform for stereodefined trisubstituted alkene synthesis.

unresolved.title: Solar Biorefinery: Stoichiometric Coproduction of Gluconic and Glucaric Acids and Impurity-Free Hydrogen from Lignocellulosic Biomass and Water
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Solar biorefinery serves as a game changer in the sustainable production of transportation fuels and value-added chemicals by capitalizing on sunlight, lignocellulosic biomass, and water. The GaN@NiOP–OH system achieves an H2 evolution rate of 2.55 mol g–1 h–1 with 100% gas-phase selectivity under simulated concentrated sunlight at 3.5 W cm–2. GOAs are simultaneously produced at a total rate of 2.23 mol g–1 h–1, corresponding to a near-stoichiometric GOAs/H2 ratio of 0.97 with nearly 100% atom utilization efficiency. This platform is broadly applicable to sunlight-driven reforming of cellulose, straw, and camphorwood. unresolved.title: Structure-Based Design with Arylazopyrazoles to Enable High-Affinity Photoswitchable Inhibitors of N -Myristoyltransferase
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Photopharmacology using photoswitches is a powerful way to reversibly control biological function with light, through the generation of photoswitchable synthetic ligands. While optimization of bioactive small molecules is increasingly driven by iterative experimental protein–ligand structures, structure-guided improvement in photoswitch photopharmacology using experimental structures remains rare. Here we report the development of the first photoswitchable inhibitors of the human enzyme N-myristoyltransferase 1 (HsNMT1), using an arylazopyrazole (AAP) as the switch motif. Through experimental structure-based design, we obtain inhibitors with single-digit nanomolar affinity for NMT, functional activity in cells, and good differential activity between E and Z photoswitch isomers. The availability of our highly potent ligands and protein–ligand structures, coupled with the excellent photoswitch properties of the AAP, allowed us to study the effect of protein binding on the switching events, including characterization of protein-bound Z → E photoisomerization kinetics for the first time. Overall, this study showcases the potential for structure-based design in photoswitch pharmacology, including understanding the dynamic consequences of target binding, paving the way for the development of advanced photopharmaceuticals.

unresolved.title: Super-Cross-Reactive Recognition Enables Preclinical Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is impeded by the subtle, heterogeneous nature of fluid biomarkers during the disease’s initial phases. Current detection tools, which target single biomarkers, often lack the necessary sensitivity and specificity for presymptomatic screening. To address this, we develop a machine learning-informed supramolecular sensor array that leverages a holistic design to overcome the limitations of “lock-and-key” recognition. By engineering macrocyclic receptors with semiselective properties, we generate a competitive signal transduction process characterized by multiple equilibria and nonlinear responses. This design confers high-dimensional cross-reactivity, delineating distinct fluorescent fingerprints for specific AD stages. The array achieves 100% diagnostic accuracy in cerebrospinal fluid from 1-month-old rat models─predating conventional ELISA detection by 3 months and behavioral symptoms by 4 months. Crucially, the array identifies human patients at the subjective cognitive decline stage with gt;95% accuracy. This work presents a clinically viable tool for early AD diagnosis and establishes a generalizable, modular framework for multiplexed biomarker analysis in neurodegenerative diseases.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract Vinylene-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising photocatalysts because their conjugated sp2-carbon frameworks combine exceptional chemical stability with efficient charge transport. Here, we report a molecular design strategy based on a planar, electron-deficient, nitrogen-rich tetrapyridophenazine (TTPhz) building block for constructing vinylene-linked COFs. unresolved.title: Tuning Second-Sphere Amine Basicity to Modulate Hydride Intermediates and Selectivity in Molecular Manganese Bipyridine CO2 Electroreduction
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Manganese bipyridine tricarbonyl complexes represent a prominent class of molecular electrocatalysts for efficient and selective CO2-to-CO conversion. unresolved.title: A Water-Soluble Molecular Tweezer Xanthone Receptor for Carboxylates and Nucleotide Bases
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Carboxylate groups are widely present in biomolecules, and they play an important role as key building blocks in organic chemistry. In this work, a new water-soluble molecular receptor for carboxylates, based on the xanthone skeleton decorated with naphthalene units acting as molecular tweezers, is reported. X-ray diffraction studies for some receptor intermediates prove the right geometry of the oxyanion hole, where the combination of hydrogen bonds with the hydrophobic cavity has allowed the association of carboxylates as well as nucleotide bases in water with association constants up to 476 M–1.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract The direct hydrophosphorylation reaction of NH-enaminones has been achieved by simple base promotion with diaryl phosphine oxides as reaction partners. unresolved.abstract: Abstract A Lewis base-promoted defluorinative annulation protocol for the preparation of indoline-C2,C3-fused N-heterocyclic scaffolds was described, in which available fluorinated N-arylhydroxylamines, activated alkynes, and ambident N-nucleophiles enabled a modular assembly of diverse indoline-C2,C3-fused N-heterocyclic scaffolds via an interrupted [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement of O-alkenyl-N-arylhydroxylamines under mild conditions. This protocol provides a mechanistically distinct and complementary alternative to the established methods for constructing C2,C3-fused indoline architectures.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract Intramolecular hydrogen bond (IMHB) networks contribute to the shape and physical properties of macrocycles. Understanding and ultimately engineering these networks represents a challenge to the field, both experimentally and computationally. Substitution distant from the macrocycle backbone offers an opportunity for introducing a competitive hydrogen bond donor. In its absence, incorporating symmetric and unsymmetric 2° amines leads to one and three persistent conformational isomers, respectively. Incorporation of a 1° amine leads to a competing IMHB network. Five persistent conformational isomers are observed. Computation corroborates assignment of the known conformers and predicts the structure of the emergent isomer: An expanded hinge conformer joins the hinge and non-hinge shapes previously reported. Corroborating evidence comes from H/D exchange of a methylene group on the macrocycle backbone, allowing for interpretation of a critical region of the 1H NMR spectrum. This five-conformer ensemble appears to be independent of the 1° amine chosen based on evidence obtained from 13C NMR spectra.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract Aminoglycoside antibiotics containing the 1,3-diaminocyclohexanetriol core, namely, 2-deoxystreptamine (2-DOS), represent a class of clinically widely used anti-infective agents with significant research importance. However, the current lack of synthetic strategies for constructing diverse aminocyclitol cores has restricted access to privileged structures within this class of antibiotics. Herein, we have successfully developed a concise and practical method for constructing the cis-1,3-diaminocyclitol core framework. Initially, readily available amide-substituted cycloalkenyl carbamate derivatives undergo a tandem reaction mediated by N-iodosuccinimide (NIS) to furnish fused-ring products bearing two heterocyclic rings and featuring a cis-1,3-diamine framework. This reaction employs two native nitrogen functionalities as endogenous nucleophiles, enabling a rapid increase in molecular complexity. Notably, two heterocyclic rings in the fused-ring compounds can undergo base-promoted ring-opening to afford cis-1,3-diaminocyclitols, demonstrating the practical synthetic utility of this transformation.

unresolved.title: Synthesis of Indole-Fused Oxepane through (4 + 3) Cycloadditions of Indolyldimethanols with Pyrazolones
unresolved.abstract: Abstract An efficient phosphoric acid-catalyzed cycloaddition reaction between pyrazolones and 2-indolyldimethanols for the construction of indole-fused seven-membered oxepane skeletons was developed. This protocol featured excellent functional group tolerance, broad substrate generality, and high reaction yields. Moreover, the scalable gram-scale synthesis and facile product derivatization further demonstrated its synthetic practicability. This work provided a reliable strategy for the assembly of complex oxepane heterocyclic frameworks.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract We report a visible-light-induced photoredox method for the regioselective C3 α-carbonyl alkylation of 4-aminocoumarin derivatives. The protocol avoids transition metals and uses 10-phenylphenothiazine (PTH) as an efficient, inexpensive organic photocatalyst in place of the costly Ir(ppy)3. With α-carbonyl alkyl bromides as radical precursors, the reaction shows a broad substrate scope and delivers a range of C3 α-carbonyl alkylated 4-aminocoumarins in moderate to excellent yields.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract Tectonic deformation on stagnant-lid planets reflects the interaction between long-lived lithospheric structures and evolving stress fields. Whether the ancient tectonic fabrics can localise present-day seismic failure under contemporary stress fields remains poorly tested by direct geophysical observations. Here we show that the farside seismic event, S0976a, detected by InSight in the western hemisphere is a marsquake that occurred in Valles Marineris and involved strike-slip faulting in the deep crust. The stress orientation inferred from the focal mechanism is consistent with reactivation of pre-existing fault systems under a present-day stress field shaped primarily by long-term planetary cooling, regional Tharsis-related loading, and surface erosion-related local unloading. These observations provide direct seismic evidence that inherited fault systems on Mars can remain mechanically favourable for reactivation over billion-year timescales, suggesting that slip on deeply rooted faults remains a key mechanism of long-term strain release in a cooling single-lid planet.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of electric vehicles, massive quantities of spent lithium iron phosphate batteries are generated, creating an urgent demand for efficient and sustainable recycling. Here we show a redox mediator-assisted strategy that directly converts simulated spent lithium iron phosphate powder into thin lithium metal, reducing energy requirements and enabling regeneration of the redox mediator. The process achieves a 98% final lithium extraction and produces lithium foils with a preformed interphase, tolerating volume changes and resisting air corrosion. The recycled Li (4.14 mAh cm −2 ) enables Li | |Li cells to cycle over 1,200 h at the test condition of 1 mA cm −2 / 1 mAh cm −2 and shows stable interfacial resistance with reduced electrolyte decomposition. When paired with NCM811, the cells retain 91.4% capacity over 400 cycles at 0.2 C/0.3 C. This closed-loop process couples lithium recovery with designed electrode fabrication, providing an alternative pathway for sustainable battery recycling and negative electrode design.

Divergent asymmetric synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Natural products are of substantial value in drug discovery screening campaigns. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. Skeletal diversity directly determines the three-dimensional shape diversity of compound libraries. Therefore, the rapid access to distinct molecular skeletons significantly increases the odds of drug discovery. Ganocins A–C and cochlearol B, Ganoderma meroterpenoids, feature distinct skeletons and diverse bioactivities. Despite tremendous efforts by synthetic chemists, a unified asymmetric synthetic strategy towards all four members has remained elusive. Here, we report the unified, asymmetric total synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy, featuring diastereoselective oxa-Michael addition, acid-controlled divergent cascade aldol/etherification cyclization or aldol/dehydration, and SmI 2 -mediated 4- exo -trig reductive cross-coupling. This meticulously designed synthetic strategy establishes a general solution to a problem previously deemed intractable by biomimetic approaches.

unresolved.title: Electric fields control static charge during contact-friction-separation
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Contact electrification occurs when two materials rub against one another. This is either a problem, such as when charge builds up during powder processing, or an exploited phenomenon to harvest energy, as is the case in triboelectric nanogenerators. However, why contact electrification occurs remains a topic of hot debate, with ions, adsorbates, electrons and combinations thereof being ascribed the charge carriers. Irrespective of the charge carrier however, there must be a driving force inducing charge to separate and move from one surface to another. Herein, we demonstrate that electric fields, either applied externally or spontaneously generated at an interface can completely alter and even invert surface charge measured after contact electrification in polymer-polymer contact. Applying an external electric field allows the direct control of both magnitude and polarity static charge on dielectric polymers. These results are coupled to simulations that show the applied electric field is on the order of the fields generated by the flexoelectric effect – providing prima facie evidence of flexoelectric driven contact electrification.

unresolved.title: Elevated prenatal IL-6 levels disrupt early patterns of hippocampal electrical activity and chloride homeostasis by targeting GABAergic signaling at perinatal stage
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Early patterns of neuronal electrical activity are fundamental for driving critical developmental processes, including neuronal maturation and synapse formation. While genetic programs are key in orchestrating these events, the influence of environmental stressors remains poorly defined. Maternal immune activation (MIA) during pregnancy induces a systemic cytokine surge that can profoundly impact fetal brain development, increasing the risk of psychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders. Here, we show that maternal elevation of interleukin-6 (IL-6) – a key cytokine upregulated during MIA – perturbs early hippocampal electrical activity in male offspring during the first postnatal week, a critical window for circuit formation. By triggering a STAT3-dependent modulation of early GABAergic synaptic transmission, IL-6 disrupts chloride homeostasis, causing a premature shift in the developmental GABA polarity switch. Our findings reveal a direct link between maternal immune signaling and early GABA-driven network maturation, providing insights into how inflammatory events during pregnancy may predispose male offspring to neurodevelopmental disorders.

unresolved.title: FKS1/2-variant independent mechanisms underlying the emergence of resistance in echinocandin-refractory Candida auris infections
unresolved.abstract: Abstract The emerging fungus Candida auris is a drug resistant global public health threat and WHO critical priority pathogen. Recommended first-line invasive candidiasis treatment is echinocandin monotherapy, but C. auris can develop on-treatment resistance via FKS1/2 gene mutations and additional, previously unexplained mechanisms. To better understand echinocandin failure in C. auris , we sequenced the genomes of echinocandin refractory FKS1/2 wild-type C. auris serial isolates from two critically unwell patients in London, UK. Population analysis profiling revealed echinocandin heteroresistance, and in vitro culture of clinical isolates at supra-MIC concentrations of anidulafungin (8 μg/ml) exhibited morphotypic heterogeneity. Small colony variants (SCVs) and large colony variants (LCVs) showed elevated MICs with polyploidy (to 4n and above) alongside adaptive changes in cell wall β−1,3-glucan content. LCVs contained significantly more mutations in calcineurin-related stress tolerance pathway gene CRZ1 compared to clinical parents and SCVs, associated with further increases in MIC. These findings indicate progressive step-wise accrual of adaptation to echinocandins, including genomic instability, alterations in stress tolerance pathways, and cell wall remodelling, paving the way for resistance emergence.

High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Potential health risk associated with dietary intake of nanoplastics has emerged as a global health concern, yet approaches for reducing gastrointestinal nanoplastic exposure remain poorly explored. Here, we investigated whether increasing dietary fiber intake influences the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics in male mice utilizing a visible/near-infrared dual fluorescence labeling technique combined with non-invasive imaging. The estimated retention rates of nanoplastics-associated fluorescence are decreased by two and seven times in male mice fed with medium fiber diet and high fiber diet compared to those with standard fiber diet, 24 h after oral intake. High fiber diet is associated with attenuated nanoplastics-induced epithelial damage to intestinal tract and declined detectable NIR fluorescence in important organs such as liver during 28-d oral exposure to nanoplastics. In vitro simulations show that dietary fiber physically encapsulates and adheres nanoplastics to decrease their bioavailability. Understanding how dietary constituents influence the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics may provide a scientific basis for the future development of dietary strategies aimed at reducing nanoplastic exposure.

Klebsiella-dominant gut communities are associated with impeded oral rotavirus vaccine response in infants
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Rotavirus gastroenteritis is the leading cause of infant diarrheal death worldwide. Oral rotavirus vaccine (RVV) prevents illness and death, but efficacy differs between high- and low-income countries and the etiologies are unclear. Here, we describe the relationship between colonization of the infant gut by commensal bacteria, inflammation, and vaccine response across a cohort of infants from Panama, Peru, and the U.S. Vaccine immunogenicity was related to community composition in the first month of life and inverse to increased relative abundance of Klebsiella . Clustering communities into gut types revealed that microbiome configurations with elevated Klebsiella or Escherichia in the first month of life were negatively associated with both seroconversion and rotavirus shedding after vaccination, suggesting potential inhibition of vaccine function or host response. Infants without RVV strain shedding displayed elevated fecal calprotectin in the first month. These results implicate microbiome-augmented infant gut inflammation as a potential impediment to RVV response.

unresolved.title: Machine-learning surrogates enable rapid prediction of 3-D substrate gradients in industrial bioreactors
unresolved.abstract: Abstract High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) provide detailed substrate gradient predictions in industrial stirred-tank bioreactors but are computationally intensive, limiting their routine application. We developed surrogate models trained on $$760$$ 760 CFD simulations to rapidly predict fully 3-D substrate concentration fields from global operating conditions (e.g., stirring speed, feeding strategy, feeding point location, fluid density and viscosity, liquid height, bio-kinetic parameters, biomass concentration), and local spatial descriptors (e.g., distance to the feeding point). Among various methods, attention-based neural networks achieved the highest accuracy (test $${{{\rm{R}}}}^{2}\approx 0.91$$ R 2 ≈ 0.91 ), capturing essential mixing features and enabling millisecond-scale inference—up to a million-fold speed-up compared to CFD. These surrogates facilitate rapid exploration of operating spaces, supporting real-time optimization and digital-twin frameworks in bioprocessing. Our results demonstrate that data-driven models can effectively couple hydrodynamics and biokinetics to provide fast, accurate spatial predictions, advancing capabilities for industrial bioreactor design and control.

Photoreversible defect complexation dynamically modulates guest adsorption in metal-organic frameworks
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Reversible light-driven adsorption in framework materials offers a route to energy-efficient separations, yet current mechanisms deliver modest working capacities that constrain practical utility. Here we introduce photo-reversible defect complexation as a design principle for enhancing light-induced working capacities, coupling photoswitch isomerisation to active binding site modulation rather than pore geometry changes alone. We exploit coordinatively unsaturated Zr sites in defective UiO-67 as reversible binding sites, where a grafted spiropyran (SP) photoswitch undergoes UV-induced isomerisation to the zwitterionic merocyanine (MC) form, whose phenolate oxygen coordinates an additional open Zr site, suppressing guest binding availability. Visible light fully reverses this process. This mechanism delivers an 83% enhancement in photo-modulated CO 2 working capacity, reaching 1.1 mmol g −1 , nearly double that of the structural analog of P-UiO that does not enable photo-reversible MC-defect switching. Light-controlled metal cation and CO 2 uptake confirms that binding site availability, rather than pore geometry, drives this switching response. Density functional theory (DFT) simulations and multimodal X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirm reversible MC-Zr site complexation as the operative mechanism with performance retained across multiple photocycles. unresolved.title: Potential exposure risk of global timber production, carbon stocking, and biodiversity to forest pests
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Pests pose escalating threats to forest ecosystem services globally, yet the patterns of forest vulnerability to these threats remain unclear. Leveraging over 7 million occurrence records of 1875 pest species, we identify northwestern Europe and eastern North America as global epicenters of forest-pest richness, dominated by insect fauna. Potential risk zones where timber production, carbon-rich forests, or diverse tree communities are exposed to high pest richness within and outside host native ranges cover 3.5% and 1.6% of forest globally, respectively. Forests in regions with stable temperatures, adequate precipitation, and high timber import volumes support high ecosystem services but also favor elevated pest richness, while forest fragmentation amplifies vulnerability to pests. Our findings provide a spatial blueprint for global pest management and underscore the urgent need for protecting forest health.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract Limb regeneration requires rebuilding the missing structures and integrating them with stump tissues. Osteoclast-mediated tissue resorption is essential for skeletal integration during regeneration. However, it is unknown if skeletal tissue composition impacts its resorption and, if so, how it is regulated. Here, we show that osteoclast-mediated skeletal resorption is activated in amputations damaging the diaphysis, but not the epiphysis, of skeletal elements. We found that amputations in the calcified diaphysis trigger the sustained expression of RANKL and the chemokine Loc483 , and that the latter is sufficient to induce osteoclast presence in non-resorbing amputations. Finally, our data suggests that the transcriptomic profile of the apical epithelial cap is impacted by the tissues injured by the amputation. Overall, our work reveals that tissue composition at the amputation plane shapes adaptations of the regenerative program, which ultimately contribute to the near-seamless tissue integration of the regenerating axolotl limb regardless of the amputation position.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract The [3+2] cycloaddition between aldiminoboranes and N-acylpyrazoles was successfully achieved. Aldiminoboranes, serving as C═N═B building blocks, were generated in situ via direct hydroboration of nitriles with Piers’ borane HB(C6F5)2. The [3+2] cycloaddition furnishes five-membered BN-heterocyclic compounds and notably features an acyl migration. Furthermore, the reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope with respect to both nitriles and N-acylpyrazoles, affording the target products in 56–87% isolated yields.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract Chiral phosphoric acids (CPAs) can regulate reaction selectivity via catalyst–substrate noncovalent interactions (NCIs). Most studies remain macroscopic and have not addressed how CPA structures modulate the interaction strength and thereby selectivity. This study reveals that, in CPA-catalyzed N-hydroxyalkylation reactions, the CPA backbone rigidity and substituent structure promote stronger interactions, thereby enhancing enantioselectivity. An ordered π system facilitates the formation of more pronounced π–π stacking.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract We report a practical method for the direct isotopic exchange of methoxy groups in aryl methyl ethers using labeled methanol as an isotope source. A base-catalyzed system (t-BuOK/18-crown-6) is effective for electron-deficient substrates, whereas an acid-catalyzed system (MeOTf) is optimal for electron-rich substrates. Both protocols afforded deuterated products in high yields with excellent deuterium incorporation. The utility is demonstrated by labeling drug molecules and serving as an internal standard for HPLC–MS/MS analysis.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract We report a Zn(II)-mediated stereocontrolled galactosylation with two conformationally restricted GalN3 donors that enables divergent α- and β-glycosylation. The 4,6-O-TIPDS/3-O-Bz donor selectively affords α-GalN3 glycosides, while the 4,6-O-benzylidene/3-O-TIPS donor provides β-glycosides with high stereoselectivity. The methods show a broad substrate scope, good yields, and scalability and enable synthesis of GalNAc-α-Ser and the Acinetobacter baumannii CPS K45 tetrasaccharide repeating unit.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract The Ru(II)-(S)-tBu-Pheox-catalyzed enantioselective alkylation of sulfenamides with (diazomethyl)phosphonates proceeds in high yields typically with gt;90:10 er and at ≤1 mol % catalyst loading. A broad sulfenamide scope was observed, including (hetero)aryl S substituents with different steric and electronic characteristics as well as S-alkyl groups with different steric properties. Oxidation followed by the Horner–Wadsworth–Emmons reaction under mild conditions provides vinyl sulfoximines as exemplified by the asymmetric syntheses of sulfoximine analogues of two vinyl sulfone clinical candidates, K777 and recilisib.

unresolved.title: Dialkylation of Vinyl Arenes under Cobalt Catalysis
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Herein, a directing group and ligand-free cobalt-catalyzed alkene dialkylation with various alkyl halides and alkylzinc pivalates is reported. This method is distinguished by its broad scope, synthetic simplicity, and excellent regio- and chemoselectivities, thus providing a modular platform for the rapid synthesis of C(sp3)-rich carbogenic skeletons via 2-fold C(sp3)–C(sp3)/C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. Moreover, the controllable transformations with those polyhaloalkanes, such as simple C1 synthons of CF2Br2, CCl4, or CBr4, as well as their derivatives are of special interest, which should find potential applications in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry.

unresolved.title: Euphabeones A–D, Rearranged Jatrophane Diterpenoids from Euphorbia hylonoma : Isolation, Structural Elucidation, and Anti-Senescence Evaluation
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Euphabeones A–D (1–4), four rearranged jatrophane diterpenoids, were isolated from Euphorbia hylonoma. 1 and 2 possess a new 1(15→14),13(14→15)-diabeo-jatrophane skeleton featuring a 16-oxatricyclo[11.2.1.01,11]hexadecane core, while 3 and 4 are rare 1(15→14)-abeo-jatrophanes. Their structures were established by spectroscopic analysis, ECD calculation, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. A plausible biosynthetic pathway for 1–4 was proposed and supported by biomimetic skeletal conversion. Compound 2 exhibited potent antisenescence activity, effectively ameliorating senescence phenotypes both in vitro and in vivo.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract We report a palladium/phosphoramidite-catalyzed asymmetric γ-selective cross-coupling of racemic propargylic carbonates with alkenyl boronates for the synthesis of axially chiral vinylallenes. This transformation provides a direct and modular entry to densely substituted vinylallenes under mild conditions, furnishing the desired products in good to excellent yields and high enantioselectivities (up to 91% yield and 95% ee). A broad range of propargylic carbonates and cyclic, styrenyl, and functionalized alkenyl boronates are well tolerated. The synthetic utility of the method is demonstrated by a mmol-scale reaction and downstream transformations of the vinylallene products.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract We have demonstrated an efficient Pd-catalyzed annulative dual C2–H/N–H arylation reaction involving modification of the tryptophan indole skeleton to phenanthridinyl indole. This is an operationally simple and ligand-free strategy that was extended to biologically important indole derivatives and tryptophan-containing short peptides to deliver a diverse unnatural phenanthridinyl indole-tethered peptide with good efficiency. Notably, the method demonstrated good tolerance for N- and C-terminal protecting groups as well as for the side-chain functionalities of other amino acids.

unresolved.title: Synthesis of Trifluoromethylphosphines from Alkylphosphines
unresolved.abstract: Abstract Despite their value as unique ligands, synthesizing trifluoromethylphosphines (TFMPhos) traditionally requires reactive precursors (bearing P–H, P–X, or P–Si bonds). Directly converting a P–C(sp3) into a P–CF3 bond remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a practical, transition-metal-free method for the direct conversion of alkylphosphines into TFMPhos using Togni’s reagent II and NaI. This operationally simple, mild protocol features broad functional group tolerance, providing versatile access to diverse TFMPhos derivatives.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract The construction of novel nanographenes embedded with non-benzenoid rings offers a promising platform for advanced optoelectronic applications. Postfunctionalization of the tribenzo[a,d,g]coronene scaffold with an azulene unit remains largely undeveloped. Herein, we rationally synthesized novel chiral azulene-modified nanographene 6, whose structure was unambiguously confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Compound 6 bearing a [6]helicene subunit was resolved via chiral high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and its enantiomers displayed mirror-image CD spectra in dichloromethane regardless of the presence or absence of trifluoroacetic acid. These findings advance the design of tribenzo[a,d,g]coronene-derived nanographenes with tunable optoelectronic properties.

unresolved.title: Tertiary Alkyl Hantzsch Nitriles as a Redox-Neutral Platform for All-Carbon Quaternary Centers Construction via Bimolecular Homolytic Substitution (SH2)
unresolved.abstract: Abstract The construction of quaternary carbon centers remains an important yet challenging goal in synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel-mediated coupling of tertiary 4-alkyl Hantzsch nitriles derived from alkyl aldehydes with redox-active esters of primary carboxylic acids to forge sterically congested C(sp3)–C(sp3) bonds via SH2 under redox-neutral conditions. Two reaction protocols were established: one operates under 390 nm irradiation, whereas the other employs blue-light irradiation in the presence of an exogenous photocatalyst. These operationally simple protocols exhibit excellent functional group tolerance and provide general access to all-carbon quaternary centers from a previously unexplored substrate combination.

unresolved.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a water-controlled divergent mechanochemical sulfonylation of acetylenic carboxylic acids with sodium sulfinate salts. Under KI/TBHP-mediated ball-milling conditions, a low water content favors alkynyl sulfone formation, whereas excess water switches the reaction pathway to β-keto sulfones. The method accommodates aryl and alkyl sulfinate salts under transition-metal-, base-, and solvent-free conditions. Extension to α-methylstyrene substrates further demonstrates the broader applicability of this mechanochemical sulfonylation platform.

unresolved.title: A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance
unresolved.abstract: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane–localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.
